title_text: The importance of holding objects while walking
content_text: Key points: - Holding objects while walking can actually improve a child’s balance, contrary to what one might think. - A study showed that 90% of 13-month-old walkers carried objects while walking without any apparent reason, and their falling decreased while doing so. - Carrying objects may give toddlers confidence and improve their balance control, while also providing an opportunity to combine manual and locomotor skills. - Surrounding objects can be put into good use for your child’s cognitive and social development while practicing walking or crawling by incorporating them into their movements. Having the chance to witness your little one’s first steps is an amazing experience! We’ve previously talked about the importance of reaching certain milestones like standing up or crawling. Today we chose a very exciting topic that’s very important when your little one is taking their first steps: pushing and pulling objects to keep balance. It may seem that holding an object while walking could be complicated for your little one. If they’re barely walking, you would think that doing two things at the same time might affect their balance. Turns out it’s exactly the other way around! Research shows that carrying an object may actually improve their balance. In a recent study, the researchers took the time to observe fifty 13-month-olds in their own homes, paying special attention to the holding of objects while walking or crawling. Turned out, walkers rarely fell while holding objects. Actually, 90% of the walkers carried objects while walking for no apparent reason and their falling decreased while doing so; they fell twice as often when not holding objects. The toddlers showed improved balance control while carrying an object. But why? A possible explanation is that holding on to something may have given them confidence. This could have a similar effect to holding on to the surface of furniture. Besides this benefit, spontaneous carrying can provide a great opportunity for children to combine manual and locomotor skills, while interacting with their environment. Here are some ways in which your little one might put surrounding objects into good use when giving their first steps: - Walking upright while carrying an object in each hand. - Walking sideways, while gripping the object in one hand and holding on to furniture for support with the other hand. - Walking while holding your hand and an object in the other hand. If your child is currently working on their crawling skills, you might observe the following carrying positions: - Crawling on hands and knees and pushing an object across the floor with one of the hands. - Carrying the object in the mouth while crawling. - Crawling while clutching the object under one arm. This is good not only for the skill of walking but for the cognitive and social development of your little one. Practicing this gives them a chance to learn about object properties and how to engage with the world in new ways. Try to have a basket with toys and objects for them to hold on to nearby!
